subject: TiltWare POC OKRs & Ops handshake
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tiltware.io>, Lisa Huang <lisa@tiltware.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: TiltWare POC — draft success metrics & timeline

Alex / Lisa — thanks again for the demo today. Quick written follow-up with a proposed POC frame so we can align owners and kick off next week if that works.

Summary (6-week POC suggested)
- Objective: Validate model quality and production economics for TiltWare's summarization + extraction flows on customer traffic.
- Duration: 6 weeks (target kickoff: week of Dec 13)

Proposed success criteria (high level)
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 220 ms for the standard 1k-token end-to-end request path (including network) under expected concurrency.
- Throughput: sustained steady-state throughput >= 350 requests/sec with short bursts to 700 req/sec.
- Cost: average cost <= $0.0025 per token produced (measured across the evaluation window).
- Quality: labelled-eval intent accuracy >= 90% on TiltWare's 5k gold set; entity extraction F1 >= 0.88.

Measurement & milestones
- Week 0 (prep): access & env decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private), sample data transfer, test tokens.
- Week 1: sandbox onboarding + sanity benchmarks (baseline latency/cost).
- Weeks 2–3: run baseline on real-ish traffic; collect metrics and run nightly evals on the 5k gold set.
- Week 4: optimizations (batching/quantization/routing) + A/B runs vs baseline.
- Week 5: stability testing at scale and cost tuning.
- Week 6: readout + decision (go/no-go & next steps).

Owners (proposed)
- Redwood infra & throughput: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — infrastructure config, load testing, capacity plan.
- Redwood quality & evals: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com) — gold set evaluation, pass/fail rubric, regression checks.
- TiltWare: Lisa to own dataset handoff and biz acceptance; Alex to coordinate procurement and environment needs.

Attachments: tiltware-poc-scope-v1.pdf (scope + baseline test plan), tiltware-sample-prompts.csv (example eval prompts). I'll also attach our standard POC checklist (redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx) in follow-up.

Key asks for you (Alex/Lisa):
1) Confirm whether you prefer Redwood Hosted API (fastest) or a Dedicated/Private deployment for this POC (if compliance/data residency matters).
2) Confirm dataset availability: you mentioned a 5k labelled gold set + unlabeled logs — can you confirm format and delivery timeline?
3) Kickoff availability week of Dec 13 (we can shift if needed).

If these look good I’ll loop in Ben/Monica to build the runbook and instrumentation. Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TiltWare POC — draft success metrics & timeline

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear frame. A few clarifying items from our side before we finalize: 

1) Environment preference: TiltWare's security team will need to confirm whether Hosted API meets our data residency and logging controls; if not, we may need a Dedicated instance (we'll confirm by Monday).
2) Traffic profile: our typical peak is ~450 rps for summarization endpoints during business hours, long-tail of smaller requests off-hours. We can provide a single-day anonymized log to illustrate distribution.
3) Gold set: we have 5,000 labelled examples ready in CSV (intent,label,entities). We also have ~1M unlabeled historical requests we can supply for calibration.
4) Procurement: looping in procurement@tiltware.io to start standard paperwork.

Two asks from our side: can Redwood's runbook explicitly call out the method you'll use to measure per-token cost (including any batching assumptions)? Also, is there a recommended eval cadence (nightly vs hourly) you prefer for the 6-week run?

If we can get those answers + a final owner list, we should be able to commit to the Dec 13 kickoff.

— Alex Turner
Head of AI Product, TiltWare

Subject: Re: TiltWare POC — draft success metrics & timeline

Rafael / Ben — I reviewed the draft and confirm Redwood can own the eval instrumentation and quality rubric. High-level plan below.

Instrumentation & measurement (what we'll capture)
- Latency: per-request histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) captured at the API gateway and at the model-serving layer so we can isolate network vs model time.
- Throughput: per-route request/sec and sustained throughput windows (5m/1h averages).
- Token accounting: per-request token input/output totals; nightly aggregation to compute avg cost/token. We will record batching parameters used during each test window.
- Quality: nightly evaluation on the 5k gold set (full-run) with per-run metrics: intent accuracy, entity precision/recall/F1, and a regression delta vs baseline. We'll also run a smaller hourly sanity check on a 500-sample subset.

Pass/fail thresholds (to be finalized with TiltWare)
- Latency: P95 <= 220 ms (measured at model-serving layer, baseline window).
- Throughput: steady >= 350 rps for a 1hr sustained window; short bursts to 700 rps allowed for 5–10 mins.
- Cost: nightly avg <= $0.0025/token (we'll show token-level breakdown and how batching impacted cost).
- Quality: intent accuracy >= 90% on the 5k gold set; entity F1 >= 0.88. Any regression > 2% on intent accuracy will trigger a triage.

Operational notes & owners
- Ben: lead for load testing and capacity gating; please confirm Dedicated lead time if TiltWare requires it.
- Rafael: customer-facing owner for acceptance and go/no-go.
- Monica (myself): owner for eval rubric, nightly reports, and final readout deck.

Next steps
1) Rafael: confirm kickoff date (aiming Dec 14 as a buffer while TiltWare confirms Hosted vs Dedicated).
2) Alex/Lisa: share the 5k gold set + one-day anonymized traffic by EOD Dec 8 so we can start baseline runs.
3) Ben: brief note on Dedicated lead time and whether the throughput/latency targets are feasible on Hosted.

Attaching tiltware-sample-prompts.csv with a small example of the expected gold-set schema. I'll produce the evaluation rubric (spreadsheet) and push to the linked drive by EOD Dec 8.

Monica
